subtitle: Ground beef with potato and carrot
verso: Grandma's picadillo: it stretches, it fills, it consoles.
story: Ground meat cooked with tomato, potato and carrot. Every family has its own, and it fills tacos dorados, gorditas, empanadas and chiles rellenos.

ingredients.title: Picadillo
items: 1½ lb ground beef (or half beef, half pork)
1 tsp salt and ¼ tsp pepper

steps: Brown the meat in the oil, breaking it up, until no pink remains. Spoon off the extra fat.
Add the onion, garlic and serrano and cook 3 minutes.
Add the tomato, cumin, salt and pepper and cook 5 minutes.
Add the potatoes, carrots and water. Cover and simmer 15 minutes until tender, adding the peas for the last 5.
Serve with rice, beans and tortillas, or use it as a filling.
pressureNote: No pressure-cooker version. Picadillo is done in 40 minutes in a skillet, and the browning is where the flavor comes from.
tips: Cut the potatoes and carrots small, about the size of a pea, so every bite gets some.

variations.name: Picadillo de Fiesta
variations.subtitle: Sweet-savory festive picadillo
variations.note: The fruit-and-nut filling for chiles en nogada, made July to September when the orchards around Puebla bear fruit. More work, and very good.

items: 1 lb ground pork plus ½ lb ground beef
½ onion and 2 garlic cloves, chopped; 3 tomatoes, blended
1 ripe plantain, 1 pear (pera de leche), 1 peach (durazno criollo) and 1 apple (manzana panochera), all diced small
¼ cup raisins and ¼ cup slivered almonds
¼ cup candied pineapple (real acitrón comes from a protected cactus)
½ tsp cinnamon and a pinch of cloves

steps: Brown the meat with the onion and garlic.
Add the tomato and cook 5 minutes.
Add the apple first, then the pear and peach, then the plantain, nuts, raisins, candied fruit and spices. Cook 15 minutes, until the fruit is tender but holds its shape.
Season with salt and a little sugar. Use to stuff roasted poblanos.
